THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment dated 18.03.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.
242/2013 by the I Addl. District Judge and Member, M.A.C.T., Chikkamagaluru ('the Tribunal' for short).

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

Brief facts of the case are, on 06.05.2012 at about 9:45 pm, the petitioner has parked his car bearing Reg.No.KA-18/M-5813 in front of Vishwa Harsha Medical Stores, another car bearing Reg.No.KA-18/M-8968 dashed on the backside of the petitioner's car completely damaging it.
The petitioner towed the vehicle to the Excel Motors, Chikkamagaluru, got it repaired by spending a sum of Rs.83,223/-.
Seeking compensation of Rs.1,93,223/- he has moved the Tribunal.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
By impugned judgment, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,000/- with 6% p.a.

Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various T.K. Harsha Vardhana vs Karthik Udupa @ Karthik on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84439756/
2 grounds.

sentences.text:
4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Yathish. J. Nadig, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. L.
Sreekanta Rao, learned counsel for the Insurance Companies.
NC: 2023:KHC:35253 5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has spent Rs.83,223/- towards the spare parts, out of which the insurer has paid Rs.20,700/-, the petitioner is entitled for the balance of compensation and also loss of income due to idling of the vehicle and the money spent by him towards conveyance and sought for enhancement of Rs.1,92,223/-.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Companies has contended that the insurer of the vehicle has already reimbursed a sum of Rs.20,700/- to the petitioner after considering the damages and money spent towards repairs.

Hence, the Tribunal has rightly considered that the petitioner is entitled only for towing charges of Rs.2,000/- accordingly and there is no ground for enhancement and he supported the impugned judgment.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, damages caused to the car in question and the petitioner is the owner of the car entitled to claim compensation.

The petitioner has relied upon the survey report under Ex.P9 said to have conducted by one Chandrashekar,
Surveyor and Loss Assessor of Chikkamagaluru.

As per the survey report, the original estimate towards labour charges is Rs.48,050/- and total parts of Rs.4,014/-, in all Rs.52,564/-, whereas the assessment is made towards the parts at a sum of Rs.4,479/- and labour charges is assessed at Rs.20,000/-, total Rs.23,479/-, whereas the Insurance Company has reimbursed a sum of Rs.20,700/-.

Even according to the argument of the Insurance Company, the own damage claim has to be reimbursed at Rs.23,479/-
NC: 2023:KHC:35253 which is excluding the towing charges, idling charges, loss of income suffered by the petitioner during the repair period.

9. On perusal of the survey report, assessment is made to the extent of Rs.5,100/- + Rs.3,850/-
towards spare parts as against Rs.12,524/-.
Labour charges is estimated at Rs.48,050/-, but assessment is made only at Rs.20,000/-.

The compensation paid to the petitioner was Rs.20,700/-
under own damage policy.
Even if the survey report is accepted, the Insurance Company is required to reimburse Rs.3,479/-, but they have paid only Rs.700/- towards spare parts which is not acceptable.
The total estimate of spare parts is Rs.12,524/-, labour charge is Rs.48,050/-, total Rs.60,574/-.
The Insurance Company has accepted the labour charges to the extent of Rs.20,000/-.

The estimated cost of labour is Rs.48,050/-, even if it is accepted at Rs.20,000/- itself, what has T.K. Harsha Vardhana vs Karthik Udupa @ Karthik on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84439756/
3 been paid towards spare NC: 2023:KHC:35253 parts is only Rs.700/- as against Rs.12,524/-
estimated in the very survey report is not acceptable.

sentences.text: Since the vehicle was not available for the petitioner during the period of repair, he has used other conveyance for which he has to be compensated.
The vehicle was kept under idling, idling charges is to be added, so also the towing charges.

Taking all these aspects into consideration, it is a fit case for award of Rs.18,000/-, it is just and proper compensation in addition to the what has been reimbursed by the insurer of the vehicle under the own damage policy.
10. I have perused the impugned judgment.

The Tribunal has not considered the above aspects, it has carried away under the impression that the insurer of the vehicle has already paid Rs.20,700/-
under own damage policy, the petitioner is entitled only for towing charges.
The survey assessment cannot be considered as the compensation is under NC: 2023:KHC:35253 third-party claim.
What are all the costs incurred by the petitioner has to be reimbursed.

Having regard to the petitioner has already obtained own damage claim of Rs.20,700/-, I am of the considered opinion that global compensation of Rs.18,000/- will adequately compensate the petitioner for the damages that the car has sustained.

Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) Impugned judgment and award is modified.
iii) The petitioner is entitled to enhanced global compensation of Rs.18,000/- with interest of 6% p.a.
iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within two NC:
2023:KHC:35253 weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the judgment.
v) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
